method.recoveryDefinition: Existing alternativeOpening simulator: first choose another visible legal opening with no more than one fewer immediate layer hit and at least60%of visible score, if available. This is a plausible deviation, not a proven mistake.
method.lastCellDefinition: lossesSolelyLastGroundCell means a lost real terminal board with score target met and exactly one green cell missing; lossesWithOneGroundCell also includes missing points.
method.terminalObservation: Passive actual-engine swap observer scoped in try/finally; synthetic sampled-model swaps have a separate prototype. Exactly one terminal observation per simulated game; observer outputs never enter a decision.
method.aggregation: Trial-weighted means of existing four-decimal simulator metrics; moves remaining on wins weighted by win count. Full-level projection retains original rows for unaffected variants.
method.informationBoundary: Policies only receive visibleState DTO. Real RNG, initial seed, history and certificates are unavailable to decisions. Sampled futures use independent bot decision seeds.
method.comparison: Matched common-seed aggregate deltas, not paired-trial win/loss discordance. Candidate rows compare only to their same published variant; projectedWholeLevel shows the effect across all four variants.
limitations: Bot rates are not human win rates; repeated deterministic trials are not independent players.
The same decision seed does not force the same move after visible board, layers or move budget change. More moves need not monotonically improve a sampled policy.
No failed bounded search is called proof of impossibility. Only replayed winning routes are certificates.
Opening-choice evaluations repeat first decisions only; they are not extra complete games.
Experimental levels have isolated lab identities and are never production attempt configurations.
Publishing changed budgets, targets, geometry or ground requires versioned base-level archives plus retained old variants/saves.
